reviews.review:
a step up from the previous game in many ways, with a few things unfortunately getting left behind. 

In terms of level design, there is much more variety in the places you will fight. The first game's general level design was 90% flat with maybe some stairs that don't really go anywhere. Not a whole lot to speak of about it. This time around, you'll be making full use of your new ability to propel yourself off the ground with your legs. You might be getting in a shootout with elves while having to hop from boat to boat at a harbor, or hopping off cliffs into invisible walls and so on. It's a shame you don't get to see most of the worlds from the first game, save for Yaesha and (kinda) Earth, but earth was the worst part of the game in the first, so i can live with that.

The gameplay has seen some tweaks that I'd say is a net positive. 
-You can now where 4 rings instead of 2, very nice.
-Set bonuses from armor was somewhat translated over in the form of archetypes, but there are some buffs and bonuses that have no equivalent in the second game, or at least I never found them. While armor is still useful, each weight class of armor kinda blends together and what you wear ends up boiling down to what looks cooler. Leto's armor set in particular was absolutely gimped from this change, which sucks :(.
-Weapons each now have a new slot for modifiers. These can augment the weapon in various ways, like returning ammo to your gun on hit, headshots light enemies on fire, faster melee, etc. They usually aren't very useful when you first get them, but with enough upgrades, they can be a pretty great boon to whatever playstyle you want.
-You now have multiple choices of Dragonheart relics that each have their own ability. Neat idea, though I'd still say the default is the most useful. There are also modifier slots for each Heart, but the bonus are so minimal that it really doesn't matter what you put on them. (wow, i can hold 1.34% more ammo, cool.) I'm sure they could eventually be useful with enough upgrades, but I beat the game and they all remained mostly useless.

The boss design in the game has gotten quite a step up as well. There aren't any world bosses that feel much like any others. They each got their own unique gimmick to them and their stages. the evil rubiks cubes and the final boss were highlights for me.

The story i find less interesting than the first, but I do like seeing the impact of the actions of the "John Remnant". More lore to learn in Yaesha and new lore for the new worlds and stuff. If you wanna ignore all that and shoot stuff, you absolutely can, but there's some neat stuff there if you care to stop and look.

One more thing, the whole game can be played Co op without any of the hassle that souls-like games tend to have. no waiting 5 minutes for your friend's summon sign to show up or having to fight a boss multiple times for each person. Just join and you're set.

In conclusion, good game with many many combinations and opportunities for synergy to suit your playstyle. I like
elden ring with guns and easier bosses( we dont talk about the final boss);
